info.title: SynapseTree Memory API (subset for @equationalapplications/mcp-server)
info.summary: Hosted shared memory for LLM agents, one SQLite database per tenant.
info.description:
SynapseTree hosts `core-llm-wiki` memory databases. Each API key reaches exactly one
tenant database; inside it, data lives in **namespaces** (the engine's `entity_id`).

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-openapi-contract-design.md`.

**Key scope.** Every operation declares `x-synapsetree-scope`: `read` operations accept
`read` and `read_write` keys; `read_write` operations refuse a `read` key with
`403 insufficient_scope`.

**Errors.** Errors produced by SynapseTree are RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` with a
stable `code`. Two responses come from the AWS API Gateway authorizer itself and keep the
gateway's native shape `{"message": "..."}`: `401` (missing or malformed bearer token) and
`403` (unknown or revoked key, or a database that is not routable).

**Writes and billing.** Writes are refused with `402 subscription_inactive` when the
organization is on a paid plan whose subscription is not `trialing`, `active` or
`past_due`. Reads always work.

**Inference is bring-your-own-key (BYOK).** SynapseTree runs no inference on its own
account: server-side extraction and semantic embeddings run against the organization's own
provider keys. Owner/admin register, rotate and delete two custodial registrations per
organization in the dashboard — an **extraction** registration (required for
`server_extraction` ingest and consolidation) and an optional **embeddings** registration —
each envelope-encrypted with KMS, never logged or echoed, surfaced only as `keyLast4`.
Rotation overwrites in place and takes effect on the next call. With no extraction
registration `server_extraction` answers `409 inference_not_configured`; a key the provider
rejects answers `409 inference_config_invalid` and surfaces as failing key health. With no
embeddings registration namespaces serve **keyword-only** search — a supported
configuration, reported via `diagnostics`, never an error. Provider calls are metered
against the plan's tier caps (one shared window, first-come-first-served); usage is
displayed as token counts, never dollars. Changing a namespace's embedding model is gated by
its stored fingerprint and takes effect only through a maintenance run
(`POST /v1/namespaces/{namespace}/maintenance/runs`); while a run is active, vector search
on that namespace pauses to keyword-only.

**Engine extensions.** `x-synapsetree-engine` names the engine entry point. Entries marked
`upstream:` depend on a core-llm-wiki API that has been requested but not yet released;
until it ships the operation or field answers `501 not_implemented`.

post.description:
Ranked top-k hybrid search (semantic + keyword) across one or more namespaces. Returns
the highest-scoring facts plus pending tasks and recent events. **Not paginated**: the
ranking is not a stable order; raise `limit` (max 100) for more results.

Semantic scoring needs embeddings. In namespaces under server extraction the query is
embedded with the organization's embeddings registration (BYOK); an organization without
one serves keyword-only search. When the embeddings path is unavailable — no
registration, a key or provider fault, the tier cap exhausted, or a maintenance run
re-embedding the namespace — the search degrades to keyword-only and reports why via
`diagnostics`. That degradation is normal operation, not an error. Alternatively pass
`queryEmbedding` (same dimension as the stored fact vectors) to supply the vector
yourself.

503.description:
Temporarily unavailable: `unavailable` (tenant cold start or writer handoff)
or `fenced` (the writer lost its lease). Upstream inference failure never
surfaces on the query path — spec §5.2 degrade-never-fail: provider trouble
degrades to keyword search with `diagnostics` instead of failing.

post.summary: Replace a fact, keeping its history
post.description:
Ends the fact's validity at `validFrom` (default: now) and makes the replacement current
from that instant. The replacement is a new mutable fact or an existing fact id.

Refused with `409 invalid_state` for `immutable_document` facts (re-ingest the document
instead), and with `409 conflict` for a fact already superseded or a replacement that
would form a cycle.

post.description:
Extracts facts from a document and stores them as `immutable_document` facts under
`sourceRef`, replacing any earlier version.

- `server_extraction`: SynapseTree runs extraction with the organization's registered
  provider key (BYOK; envelope-encrypted, managed in the dashboard by owner/admin).
  `409 inference_not_configured` when the organization has no extraction registration.
- `client_extraction`: the client ran the extraction itself against an
  [extraction plan](#operation/createExtractionPlan) and posts each chunk's model
  output. A plan whose fingerprint no longer matches is refused with
  `409 extraction_plan_stale`.

409.description:
The write conflicts with current state: `conflict`, `extraction_plan_stale`,
`source_hash_conflict` (another sourceRef already holds this content hash),
`namespace_busy` (the namespace is under another write; retry),
`inference_not_configured` (server extraction requested but the organization has
no extraction registration), or `inference_config_invalid` (the provider rejected
the organization's key as configuration-invalid — auth or bad option — on every
extraction call; nothing was written and the response is not retried).

value.detail: Another sourceRef in this namespace already holds this content.

value.detail: The provider rejected the tenant's model key as configuration-invalid on every extraction call; nothing was written.

422.description:
Well-formed but refused: `ontology_violation`, `ingest_failed`,
`idempotency_key_reused`, `embedding_dimension_mismatch` (client vector with a
different dimension), or `embedding_model_mismatch` (the tenant's configured
embedding model differs from the namespace's stored-vector fingerprint; the
refusal precedes any write and points at the re-embed maintenance path).

value.detail: Node type "microservice" is not in this namespace's strict manifest.

value.title: Embedding model mismatch
value.detail: The configured embedding model differs from the namespace's stored-vector fingerprint; run maintenance to re-embed.

503.description:
Temporarily unavailable: `unavailable` (tenant cold start or writer handoff),
`fenced` (the writer lost its lease; the write did not commit), or
`upstream_inference_unavailable` (the tenant's inference provider failed on
every extraction call, or either BYOK rate cap (extraction or embeddings)
is exhausted for the window (429/5xx/timeout; nothing was written; safe
to retry)). When the embeddings rate cap is exhausted by an active
maintenance run, the problem `detail` names the run (`mrun_…`) as the
consumer.

value.detail: The write did not commit; retry.

value.detail: The tenant's inference provider failed on every extraction call (429/5xx/timeout); nothing was written.

post.summary: Traverse the graph from an anchor fact
post.description:
Walks edges from `sourceId` up to `maxDepth` hops (1–3). The anchor is always returned
first; discovered nodes follow in depth order. Only edges whose both endpoints are
returned are included. With `asOf`, only facts live at that instant are walked.
Bounded by `maxNodes`; not paginated.

post.summary: Start agent registration for an email
post.description:
First step of auth.md agent registration: an agent without an API key
asks SynapseTree to email the human a claim link. The endpoint is
unauthenticated; the response is byte-equal for known and unknown
emails (anti-enumeration). At most 5 claim tokens may be outstanding
for one email — the 6th answers `quota_exceeded` (an existing
ProblemCode; errors here are problem+json only). Success returns the
`stclaim_…` claim token the agent polls with, a short `user_code` the
human confirms on the consent interstitial, and the poll parameters. The
outstanding-token cap responds `quota_exceeded`.

200.description:
The claim is pending; a confirmation email is on its way to the
human. Byte-equal whether or not the email is known to SynapseTree.

post.summary: Poll the claim grant for the minted API key
post.description:
Device-flow style poll (RFC 8628 §3.4/§3.5) with a claim grant: the
agent presents the `stclaim_…` token from POST /agent/identity as the
`assertion` (RFC 7523 jwt-bearer shape) with grant type
`urn:synapsetree:claim`. Before the human approves, the endpoint
answers `authorization_pending` (with `interval`) or `slow_down`;
after approval the FIRST poll mints exactly one API key (and, in the
same transaction, frees the claim token) and answers with it — later
polls answer `invalid_grant`, as do expiry and absence. If the
organization already holds 10 live agent keys the poll answers
`key_limit_reached`, a documented extension of the RFC 6749 §5.2
`error` member (not a problem+json code). Errors here are RFC 6749
§5.2 bodies, never problem+json. No per-IP rate limit exists in v1.

200.description:
The claim was approved and redeemed; exactly one API key was
minted. Polling again answers `invalid_grant`.

post.description:
RFC 7009 revocation, bearer-authenticated like every other key-bearing
endpoint. Revoking an agent key frees its seat against the
organization's 10-key cap. The endpoint answers 200 on every
request carrying a LIVE bearer — the response is byte-equal whether the
token was revoked or was unknown. A revoked, deleted or unknown CLIENT
bearer never reaches the handler: the edge answers 401 (the shared
`unauthorized` problem, RFC 6750 — byte-equal for unknown and revoked
bearers, anti-enumeration). A request with an ABSENT or MALFORMED
`Authorization` header is refused by the API Gateway authorizer before
the handler runs, with the gateway's default native body
`{"message":"Unauthorized"}` (not problem+json, no `WWW-Authenticate`
challenge). Errors from the handler are RFC 6749 §5.2 bodies, never
problem+json (the two 401 bodies above excepted).

200.description: The token is revoked, or was unknown; byte-equal either way. Requires a live bearer.

401.description:
The CLIENT bearer is unknown, revoked or invalid (RFC 6750). Emitted by the
application's shared 401 emitter, byte-equal to the pool's — anti-enumeration
(unknown and revoked bearers are indistinguishable). A missing/malformed
`Authorization` header instead yields the API Gateway default 401 body
`{"message":"Unauthorized"}` — see the operation description.

Namespace.description: A namespace inside the tenant database (the engine's entity_id).

OauthErrorBody.description:
RFC 6749 §5.2 error body: `error` plus optional `error_description`;
`interval` rides on `authorization_pending` (RFC 8628 §3.5).
`key_limit_reached`, `database_name_taken` and `database_quota_exceeded`
are documented SynapseTree extensions of the `error` member — account
walls a human must clear, after which the agent resumes polling (the
claim grant survives until its TTL):
`key_limit_reached` (the organization's 10-key cap — prune keys in the
dashboard), `database_name_taken` (the default database name is held by
a deleted database until GC cleanup — create a differently-named
database in the dashboard), `database_quota_exceeded` (the plan has no
free database slot — delete a database or upgrade, then poll again).
They are error-member values here, not problem+json ProblemCodes.

error.description: An RFC 6749 §5.2 code, an RFC 8628 §3.5 code, or a documented SynapseTree extension (`key_limit_reached`, `database_name_taken`, `database_quota_exceeded`).

error_uri.description: Optional RFC 6749 §5.2 pointer to the dashboard page that clears the wall.

interval.description: Seconds to wait before polling again (RFC 8628 §3.5).

OkfType.description:
Ontology node type. Open: each namespace's manifest defines its own types and `emergent`
mode adds more; facts imported from OKF bundles keep their original type string. The
listed values are the schema-software-org types.

OnDuplicateHash.description: When another sourceRef already holds this content: `skip` (write nothing), `ingest` anyway, or `error` (409 source_hash_conflict).

PollGrant.description: Where and how to poll for the minted key.

grant.description: The claim-grant type to send as `grant_type`.

interval.description:
Minimum seconds between polls of `token_endpoint` (the RFC 8628 §3.2
placement, ruled 2026-11-01). An `authorization_pending` or
`slow_down` answer may carry a larger `interval`, which replaces
this one from then on.

duplicateOf.description: The sourceRef already holding this content (`source_hash_conflict`).

ProblemCode.description:
Stable machine-readable error code. Open: new codes may be added in minor versions, so
clients must treat an unlisted code as a generic error of its HTTP status. The listed
values are the codes this version defines.

QueryDiagnostics.description:
Named BYOK diagnostics for a query response. A typed map: keys are diagnostic
names, values are scalars; unknown names are legal and clients must ignore them.
Reported reasons include `keyword_only: true` (the organization has no embeddings
registration) and `embed_unavailable: <reason>` (key or provider fault, or the tier
cap exhausted). While a maintenance run holds the namespace, vector search is
paused and reads answer keyword-only; the run itself is surfaced through
`currentRunId` and `currentRunState` on the pending-maintenance object. All of
these are normal keyword-only degradation, not errors.

additionalProperties.description: A named diagnostic flag, count or label.

query.description: Search text. Empty returns the most recent facts.

hybridWeight.description: 0 = keyword only, 1 = semantic only. Omit for the default semantic ranking.

asOf.description: Return facts that were true at this instant, using current knowledge.

weights.description: Per-namespace score multipliers (default 1; 0 skips the namespace).

floors.description: Minimum results reserved per namespace before the global `limit` cut.

tokenBudget.description: Pack facts into this many estimated tokens.

scores.description: Score per returned fact id (empty for recency reads).

diagnostics.description:
Additive BYOK diagnostics; present only when there is something to report
(e.g. the searched namespaces serve keyword-only facts because the org has
no embeddings registration).

token.description: The API key to revoke (revocation is defined for keys only).

SourceHash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the source's bytes.

SourceRef.description:
Identifies one source document within a namespace. Restricted to characters the engine
stores unchanged; the SDK's `toSourceRef(path)` encodes `/` as `__`.

SourceType.description: How a fact was produced. `immutable_document` facts change only by re-ingesting their source.

validFrom.description: When the old fact stopped being true and the replacement became true. Defaults to now.

TokenResponse.description: RFC 6749 §5.1 success response — exactly one freshly minted API key.

access_token.description: The minted API key. The only time it is ever shown.

token_type.description: RFC 6749 §5.1 — keys authenticate as bearer tokens.

account_id.description: The organization the key belongs to (its `account_id` context).

scope.description: Agent keys always carry the full memory scope.

edgeTypes.description: Allowed edge types. Omit for all; an empty array matches none.

nodes.description: Anchor first, then neighbours by depth.

UserConfirmedFact.description: A fact a user has confirmed.

UserStatedFact.description: A fact stated directly by a user or agent.
